question.text: During pre-registration due diligence, Ms. Priya Shah (SIA) discovers that Hariyali Foundation (environment NPO) received an Income-Tax scrutiny notice 15 days ago for FY 2022-23 alleging misuse of Section 11 application. The CEO wants to hold off disclosing until the final order. What is the CORRECT position per Table 3.1 (Exemption under Income Tax Act row)?

answer.text: Pending notices or scrutiny cases from all regulatory and statutory authorities shall be DISCLOSED at the time of making the application; fines/penalties if imposed must be disclosed as paid or appealed within 7 days.
Silence is fine — disclosure is needed only after an adverse order.
Only fines above Rs. 1 crore need to be disclosed.
Disclosure is required only on BSE SSE, not NSE SSE.

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 3.1 ('Exemption under Income Tax Act' row) states: 'Details regarding pending notices or scrutiny cases from all regulatory and statutory authority shall be disclosed at the time of making the application for the registration. Fines or penalties if imposed shall be disclosed as paid or appealed within 7 days.' The Stock Exchanges RESERVE THE RIGHT to refuse registration if the notices/scrutiny cases are grave enough to endanger the 12A status. The Trap: Option A advocates non-disclosure — directly contrary to regulation. Option C adds a fabricated materiality threshold. Option D creates a false NSE/BSE split (both SSEs apply the same SEBI circular). Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C (Compliance) test material-event disclosures under LODR Reg 30. X-A (IA) covers disclosure of regulatory actions. XXIII specifically tests the PRE-REGISTRATION disclosure duty. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build a 'Regulatory Litigation Log' for the SIA working file: one row per notice/show-cause/assessment, with date of receipt, current status, and disclosure date to SSE. The 7-day clock for fines/penalties is tight — set alerts. SIAs often miss this and issue clean opinions on contingently-damaged NPOs.
